source.citation: Richet, P., Bottinga, Y. (1986). Thermochemical properties of silicate glasses and liquids: a review. Reviews of Geophysics 24(1), 1-25.

transcription.from: the published article (publisher's PDF), Table A1 read on the page rendered at 200 dpi, with the reference letters of its footnotes
transcription.note: Only the enthalpies of vitrification are transcribed (columns Ts, Delta Hv(Ts) and Reference); the fusion columns of the table are not. An uncertainty the table does not print is null. The table compiles measurements by solution calorimetry: at 295-298 K in an aqueous solvent, near 970-985 K in an oxide melt. For CaSiO3 at 298 K the crystal is pseudowollastonite (Richet and Bottinga 1984, Table 6).
